sections.h2: How does selling a house in Peachtree City, GA work?
sections.html:
Most Peachtree City sellers weigh a standard listing against a private sale or a cash offer, and what sets this market apart is that your house comes with access to a path system, a village identity and, sometimes, a registered golf cart. The Census Bureau counts 40,880 residents on July 1, 2025, a 6.9% rise from the 38,241 in its April 2020 base.

The Census 2020 to 2024 survey describes a high-ownership city: 72.1% of housing units are owner occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $482,500, median household income is $113,987 and 61.6% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Median gross rent is $2,086, which matters if a buyer is deciding between renting and purchasing. About 21.0% of residents are 65 or older, and the city's land area is 25.14 square miles in the Census count.

sections.h2: What is Peachtree City's layout, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Peachtree City was chartered on March 9, 1959, after a group of developers gathered more than 12,000 acres in Fayette County for a planned community. The plan divided the city into villages, each with its own shopping, recreation and elementary school. Today's villages are Aberdeen, Braelinn, Glenloch, Kedron and Wilksmoor. The original plan assumed between 80,000 and 110,000 residents, and a 1985 revision lowered the build-out target to about 45,000.

The city sits in Georgia's Piedmont, with elevations from 740 to 961 feet, and has three lakes: Lake Peachtree at about 270 acres, Lake Kedron at about 240 acres and Lake McIntosh at about 650 acres. When you describe the house to buyers, name the village and the nearest path connection, since both shape how people picture daily life here. McIntosh High School carries the name of the Creek chief whose land cession shaped the county.

sections.h2: How do golf cart paths and cart registration affect a sale?
sections.html:
The city advertises more than 100 miles of shared-use paths and about 11,000 registered motorized carts. A seller who owns a cart has paperwork to finish, and a buyer who plans to buy one needs to know the rules. The city's cart page sets out the following:

  • New cart registrations are completed in person at City Hall, and owners must be 18 or older.
  • A cart must be registered within 10 days of purchase.
  • A seller must report the sale or removal of decals within 10 days using the Cart Release Form.
  • A move requires a change of address notice within 60 days.
  • Decals must now appear on both the front and rear of the cart.

Cost depends on residency. Residents pay a $45 renewal covering 2026 through 2028. Buyers who live outside the city and do not pay Peachtree City property taxes pay a yearly path user fee on top of registration:

Peachtree City motorized cart charges
ItemAmount as printed by the city
Decal$15 per year
Ownership transfer$15
Path user fee for owners outside the city$235 per year
Registration plus path fee, outside owners$250 per year

Source: City of Peachtree City, Paths and Motorized Carts page.

sections.h2: Can a buyer run a short-term rental from a Peachtree City house?
sections.html:
Only with a city permit. Since January 1, 2025, every short-term rental, defined as lodging of 30 consecutive days or less, needs one, and the city capped total permits at 135. Applicants who could document operating and paying taxes before the ordinance was adopted on November 7, 2024 had priority. If the existing rentals exceed 135, all of them are permitted and no new permits issue until the count falls below the cap.

Rentals are allowed in residential zoning districts, but detached structures, guest houses, recreational vehicles and trailers cannot be rented this way. A permit lasts 730 days. Applicants provide:

  • The completed application and a guest occupancy agreement under O.C.G.A. 43-21-3.2
  • A copy of the deed showing the applicant owns the property
  • A notarized criminal background check consent and a notarized tax payment and ordinance affidavit
  • Homeowner association approval, if one applies

The Building Department and Fire Marshal also inspect the property. Fines escalate for repeat violations, and a third one in 12 months can mean revocation for 24 months. If your house is being marketed as an income property, ask the city's planning staff whether the permit stays with the owner or the address before you tell a buyer it transfers.

sections.h2: How are Peachtree City property taxes assessed and appealed?
sections.html:
Fayette County's Assessors' Office values real and personal property and takes homestead applications. The Tax Commissioner handles billing and collection, and the Assessors' page lists that office at 770-461-3652. For 2026, residential and commercial notices were mailed June 23, and the appeal deadline of July 7, 2026 has passed. Each year's notice opens a new 45-day appeal window, and the written appeal must be signed, dated and received inside it.

One Fayette change helps buyers: homestead applications are no longer cut off on April 1. If you owned and occupied the home on January 1, you can apply up to the end of that year's appeal window. Someone who moved in later applies after the next January 1. A recently purchased home needs a recorded warranty deed or settlement statement along with a Georgia driver's license showing the address.

Fayette's exemption page lists several tiers that a seller can point buyers toward:

  • The basic L1 homestead exemption reduces state and school M&O assessed value by $2,000 and county and fire M&O by $5,000.
  • The L7 floating exemption limits yearly growth of the school portion of a homesteaded value to the lesser of 3% or inflation, plus improvements.
  • Owners 62 by January 1 may qualify for a school tax reduction that rises from $2,000 to $4,000, and owners 65 may qualify for a 50% school tax reduction.
  • A 100% disabled veteran may qualify for an exemption of $126,526.

Call the Fayette Assessors at 770-305-5376 for the codes on your bill.

sections.h2: What does Georgia charge to transfer a Peachtree City house?
sections.html:
Georgia's transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 of the price and 10 cents for each further $100 or fraction of $100. It must be paid before the clerk of superior court records the deed, and the clerk then certifies payment on the document. The law makes the seller liable, though sales contracts commonly make the buyer responsible. The electronic PT-61 is filed through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, which takes questions at (800) 304-5174.

Ask the Fayette County clerk of superior court for the current recording fee schedule, and ask your closing attorney to confirm the tax lines on the settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Peachtree City?
sections.html:
Houses in good condition inside popular villages usually do well on the open market, because buyers are drawn to the path network and the lakes. Listing means preparation, showings and negotiation over inspection items. A private sale cuts the commission but leaves marketing and contracts to you.

A cash buyer fits sellers who face a deadline, inherited a house, or own a property that needs more repair than a lender will finance. Cash buyers purchase as-is, so the price reflects their repair and resale costs. Ask each buyer for written terms, check who pays transfer tax, and decide with your closing attorney how the cart registration and any rental permit will be handled at transfer.

faqs.q: Do I have to transfer my golf cart registration when I sell my Peachtree City house?
faqs.a: Yes if the cart is leaving with the house. The seller must report the sale or remove the decals within 10 days, and the buyer must register within 10 days of purchase. Use the city's Ownership Release and Cart Release forms and visit City Hall in person.

faqs.q: How many short-term rental permits does Peachtree City allow?
faqs.a: The ordinance caps permits at 135 citywide. Existing operators who documented their rentals before November 7, 2024 had priority, and permits renew every 730 days. Ask the city whether a permit can follow a property to a new owner.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 appeal window still open for Peachtree City owners?
faqs.a: No. Fayette's 2026 residential and commercial appeal deadline was July 7, 2026. Each future notice opens a new 45-day window, so file within it. Call the Assessors' Office at 770-305-5376 for questions.

faqs.q: Can a new owner get a homestead exemption after the April 1 date?
faqs.a: Fayette now accepts applications until the end of the 45-day appeal window for that year, as long as the owner lived in the home on January 1. A recorded warranty deed or settlement statement and a Georgia driver's license are required for a recent purchase.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia transfer tax on a Peachtree City sale?
faqs.a: By law the seller is liable, though many contracts assign it to the buyer. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each extra $100 or fraction of $100, paid before the deed is recorded.
